subject.title: Skipped group messages behind requireMention do not reach message hooks, which blocks full-history archive plugins

question: Should trusted installed plugins be allowed to passively observe inbound group messages skipped by mention gating through a public Plugin SDK hook, and should that visibility require an explicit operator/plugin gate?
rationale: This changes the public plugin privacy boundary by exposing content before the current mention/session dispatch gates would make it visible to plugins.

options.title: Gate the public hook
options.body: Add an explicit operator or plugin-permission gate, document the payload boundary, and land the hook only after that contract is visible.

options.title: Approve installed-plugin trust
options.body: Accept that installed plugins registering the hook may observe skipped inbound content without an additional gate.

options.title: Keep internal ingest only
options.body: Reject or pause the public hook and leave full-fidelity archive plugins dependent on internal or channel-specific integrations for now.

recommendation.title: Gate the public hook
recommendation.body: Add an explicit operator or plugin-permission gate, document the payload boundary, and land the hook only after that contract is visible.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the nearest shipped skipped-message ingest behavior and are the clearest history owner for deciding whether that internal boundary becomes public.
